[LCST.4.1.3] **`NULLABLE` binds to the target.** The optional `?` in `cast_suffix` must
bind to the immediately preceding `TYPE_SYM` and must be consumed as part of the cast
before any following operator is considered — `x::Int?` is a fallible cast whose `?`
cannot be stolen by a following operator. Because `??` (COALESCE) is a single token under
maximal munch ([LLEX.10.8.5]), `x::Int??d` lexes as `x :: Int ?? d` and parses as
`(x::Int) ?? d` — a **total** cast then coalesce, with no `NULLABLE` on `Int`. The
fallible-then-coalesce idiom is therefore written with the target `?` separated from the
`??`: `x::Int? ?? d` → `(x::Int?) ?? d`. *(No whitespace-free spelling of the fallible
idiom exists — `x::Int???d` mis-munches — so a fallible cast that then coalesces must
separate the target `?` from the `??`; a total cast on a nullable source is instead the
`[LCST.4.3]` missing-`?` error, which guides the author to the spaced form.)*
